B. Is this measure already running in Central Finland wellbeing services county (or in the KYS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Video MDT review of every stage I-III patient with the university hospital. Every patient whose cancer has not spread (stage I-III) is discussed by video with the university hospital lung team (surgeon, radiotherapy doctor, oncologist) before anyone decides against treatment that aims to cure. Today a county hospital can decide alone.
supported_en: One UK district hospital before-after study (J Telemed Telecare 2004, 62 patients) reports a 30% relative rise in the yearly surgery rate after video team meetings began.
not_supported_en: No page measures the change in the share of all patients who get curative treatment, and none shows the gain in a county whose surgery share is already high.
summary_en: Central Finland's care pathway page (hyvaks.fi) says every new lung cancer patient is discussed in a local team meeting with a lung doctor, surgeon, oncologist and radiologist. No page found mentions a video review with KYS, and KYS's 2021 care pathway describes only its own weekly meeting. For the effect, one 2004 UK district hospital study reports that the yearly surgery rate rose 30% (relative) after video team meetings began. The Finnish Cancer Registry (2024) reports that 23.7% of Central Finland's male patients had surgery, against 12.6% nationally.
unanswered_en: No page says whether KYS doctors join Sairaala Nova's lung team meeting by video, or whether this is planned in the collaborative-area agreements.
